incident-bot: PAGED #eng-oncall: high-error-rate on batcher-pool-us-east (pager: P2) — incidents/INC-2026-447

Sam Nguyen: Early AM handoff. Quick summary of last 12h and current status.
- Primary: Sam (this shift)
- Secondary: Priya (on-call)
- Coverage gap: low staffing 03:00-05:00 UTC; we routed extra traffic to fallback region but saw 10-15% increased latency for sessions >1024 tokens.

What happened:
- 00:42 UTC: batcher nodes in us-east started OOM-killing batcher-worker pods under sustained long-generation load.
- 00:45 UTC: alerting triggered (error-rate, eviction spikes). incident-bot paged oncall.
- 00:50 UTC: Kai restarted affected nodes and adjusted kube-scheduler eviction thresholds as a short-term mitigation.
- 01:30 UTC: We rolled a targeted config change to reduce max_batch_size from 512 -> 256 for the affected pool which stabilized memory usage.

Current status (as of last check 04:00 UTC):
- batcher-pool-us-east: healthy, 3/3 pods Ready, memory pressure reduced to normal.
- No customer-facing 5xx anymore. A minority (~0.6%) of requests experienced higher latency during the window.
- Root cause suspected: a combination of long context lengths + a suboptimal KV-cache memory accounting bug (see follow-up).

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Reduced max_batch_size on us-east pool (config id: cfg-8332).
- Restarted two nodes and drained temporary hot pods.
- Canary traffic shifted to us-west for large-context requests (>1024 tokens) for 90 minutes.

Commands / logs used during triage:
```
# check batcher pods and memory
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=batcher -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs batcher-worker-7ff4 -c batcher | tail -n 120
# quick check for OOMs
kubectl -n inference describe pod batcher-worker-7ff4 | grep -i oom
```
Log excerpt:
```
I 00:41:22 [batcher] eviction: process memory exceeded threshold, evicting cached-kv  (size=12.1GB)
E 00:41:25 runtime: out of memory allocating 256MB
```

Runbook pointers:
- Primary runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batcher-oom
- Quick mitigation checklist: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/batcher-hotfix
- If you need to shift traffic: https://redwood.internal/ops/traffic-reroute

Open follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- [Priya] Confirm root cause by reproducing workload in staging and capture heap profile (ETA: today EOD).
- [Kai] Submit PR to fix KV-cache accounting and run perf tests (ETA: 48h).
- [Zach] Capacity plan for us-east pool to avoid recurrence during sustained large-context runs (ETA: next Monday).

Notes for next shift:
- Primary handoff -> Priya at 08:00 UTC. Sam will be available for 1hr overlap.
- Keep an eye on allocations for sessions >1024 tokens in us-east. Alert threshold: sustained mem_pressure > 70% for 5m.
- If latency > 800ms for more than 3% of requests, escalate to P1 and follow the traffic-shift runbook.

Priya Patel: Thanks Sam — I’ll pick this up at 08:00 UTC. I ran a quick smoke in staging using the long-context script and saw similar memory delta but couldn't trigger OOM so far. I’ll get heap profiles asap.

Kai Huang: FYI I left a temporary note in the cluster annotation: "batcher:max_batch_size=256;reverted_on_stable" so ops automation can see it. PR draft for kv-accounting in my fork, will tag reviewers shortly.

Zach Martin: Capacity ask noted. I’ll propose a short-term reserve of +2 nodes for the pool (non-preemptible) and a longer-term autoscale rule change. Will share numbers by EOD Monday.

Priya Patel: Quick check item — are there any customer escalations? I did a sweep and found two PRO accounts with degraded latency during the window, reached out and they acknowledged the mitigation. No legal/compliance flags.

Sam Nguyen: Good. For handoff:
- Priya, you’re primary. Kai secondary for infra changes. Zach for capacity/purchase decisions.
- Paging rules: keep pager policy unchanged unless you see >3% errors across regions.

Priya Patel: A couple of operational notes for next shift:
- If you see `eviction: process memory` logs, toggle the following in staging first:
  - decrease max_batch_size
  - bump kv-cache eviction aggressiveness
- I’ll add a one-line summary to the runbook with the exact kube commands I used.

Kai Huang: Also added cluster-level metric: `batcher.big_ctx_allocs` which should help detect before OOM. Alert will go to #eng-monitoring and pager after 2m sustained.

Sam Nguyen: Last thing — tagging this thread as the official handoff record for today. Priya please update the runbook link with reproduction steps and attach heap profile when you have it.

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-447 closed (summary: mitigated by config change and node restarts). Resolution note: temporary config change applied; follow-ups in thread.

Priya Patel: Acknowledged. I’ll update first_message_ts notes and add heap_profile link here when ready.

Zach Martin: Leaving a short checklist for next oncall:
- verify cluster annotations cleared after revert
- confirm PR merged and deployed to canary
- update capacity plan in Confluence

Sam Nguyen: Thanks all, handing off — Priya you're up. :wave:

Priya Patel: taking over :raised_hands: — will post EOD summary.
